Selection and Interview Process at Capgemini

The interview process at Capgemini typically comprises three to four rounds, starting with a Phone screening or aptitude assessment, then technical round, proceeding to a HR interview for applicable roles.

1. Application & Shortlisting: Candidates apply either through the company’s official portal or via campus recruitment. The submitted resume is reviewed during the initial screening process. If shortlisted, recruiters may reach out for a screening call to assess basic qualifications, communication skills, and interest in the role.

2. Online Assessment: Depending on the hiring drive, candidates may be required to complete an online assessment. This stage can vary and is not always mandatory. Aptitude / Logical Reasoning Test includes multiple-choice questions covering quantitative ability, logical reasoning, and verbal skills. Technical / Pseudocode Test includes questions focused on programming fundamentals, basic coding logic, output-based problems, and IT concepts.

3.Technical Interview: This interview primarily evaluates core technical knowledge and practical understanding. Common focus areas include programming fundamentals in languages such as Java, Python, or C++, along with object-oriented programming concepts like inheritance and polymorphism. Interviewers may also assess basic knowledge of databases, particularly SQL, as well as fundamental concepts of operating systems and DBMS. In addition, candidates are expected to clearly explain the projects listed on their resume and demonstrate their role and contributions.

4. HR / Behavioral Interview: Assessing a candidate’s soft skills, communication ability, and overall cultural fit with the organization. During this round, candidates are commonly asked to introduce themselves and discuss their resume, explain their motivation for choosing Capgemini, and talk about their strengths and weaknesses.

Basic Interview Questions

  • Tell me about yourself.
  • What are your strengths and weaknesses?
  • Describe your ideal work environment.
  • How do you handle criticism or feedback?
  • What are your salary expectations?
  • Why do you want to work here?
  • What motivates you to perform well at work?
